projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Gaeton Lanese was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: This is the oral history of World War II veteran Gaeton A. Lanese. Mr. Lanese served in the U.S. Army Air Corps with the 15th Air Force, 99th Bomb Group, 416th Squadron. He served in the Mediterranean and European theaters, and his highest rank was staff sergeant. I'm Tom Swope, and this interview was recorded at Gaetano's restaurant in Mayfield Heights, Ohio, on March 7th, 2005. Gaeton was 81 at the time of this recording. Where -- where were you living in 1941?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: In Lyndhurst? How old were you in '41?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Do you have specific memories of the day the Japanese attacked Pearl Harbor?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Well, I don't know too much -- when that happened where I was? I was in high school.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I was at Brush. That's where I was.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How did you hear the news on that day, do you remember?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: They announced it over the -- in -- in the school.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And then we all -- they had called it and, you know, all the kids had emptied all the rooms and everything, and we went home, and that's the way it ... Then when it come time for the sign-up, we were drafting, you know, they come -- all the sudden they come, you know, and then the guys come, Hey, look, my -- his paper. Yeah, geez. You know, they thought that was big time. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. Well, they did. And I says, Geez, I don't know, I didn't get mine yet. Because we were on Sheffield (ph) so I called the house, talked to my mother. I said, Get the mail. Did I get the papers, you know. Yeah, you got them. Oh. I told them, Hey, I got them. I thought that was happy.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So that was your draft notice.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So did you then -- did you -- were you drafted or did you go out and sign up?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You wanted to get into the Army Air Corps?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So when did you do that?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: What in the hell was it? It would be in there. I'll tell you where I'm at. In my thing.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: All right. We've got a little book here with a --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. What -- when we arrived, where we went first, where we went.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You went -- do you remember when you went into the Army Air Corps, though? Was that 1943? Is that when you went in?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. I think and I saw it on my discharge. I was looking for it yesterday and I saw it on there that it was '44. A couple things, it -- with the school and everything, you know, and I think it says 19 -- this and 1944, 1944.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So what can you tell me about your training?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Well, I was -- went to -- I was in Florida -- Florida. I was in -- down south in --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Payson. Payson. Gee, I can't even remember when --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You know, it comes. It delays, and talking it comes.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Yeah. If you can tell me about your training.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. Went to Miami, and I -- down there I was broke in. We were working in the -- in the C -- in the -- in the damn ___.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you have basic training or --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I don't know if it would be engineer or what you want to call them, you know.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And I had that. I didn't -- we -- going down we didn't know where in the hell we were going. They didn't tell us nothing, you know, and geez, where are we going? Here we ended up -- all the time I was in the service I was down there in the winter.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Even when I was overseas and with this, come back, always in there every -- I never had a one. Even at the end ___. The end of the war and everything when I was getting discharged, I was down there in St. -- big port, what the hell that was.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So why did you decide on joining the Army Air Corps?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I didn't -- boy, they sent me there.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. Nobody knew where the hell we were getting -- you know, where we were going.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Everybody was looking out trying to see where we stopped.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And I just -- we just went in in California for a minute and back out and then we went up to Utah.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: That's where they made up the place, the gangs.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Now, did you -- did you want to become a pilot?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You would rather be in the crew somewhere?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you became a waste gunner, right?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Where did you go to gunnery school?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: It's a school, if you want to call it, or what. That's where you go to open ___ -- open AT-6, and you go with the -- pulling the ___, what the hell you call them, for the gun.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You know? Break you in. So we got pretty good. We had one occasion there that the -- you're going and the pilots calls the guy in the back, because there's two on that, you know, the guy and -- and so you're looking at that, and so all of a sudden he yells at the guy again and he said -- you know, he looked out, he saw there was a parachute going down, you know, and he tried to ___+, that guy, he hit. After he hit he wanted to know what the hell he did, why he bailed out, you know. He says he -- he was shooting, and he says, I thought you -- you had said that -- I told -- you told me to save my ass. He says, No, I said save the brass.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, he said I had -- so ... Then we had another occasion, the -- well, we were in Utah there, and this -- you know, he was a chief of police here.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You know -- what the hell was his name? Back -- then he went to -- he went to horse -- race horses and that. Nick -- Nick Tagg (ph).

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, he was one of the relatives of ours, yeah. His picture's in there on the wall, too.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Yeah, I met somebody else who met Nick Tagg.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. So ___+. Where the hell -- where were we? Oh, we went --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: So we were up there and I caught up to him, see, and he went in a month ahead of me, and I get over there and here he is. You know, I says, How the hell did you get ahead of me? He said he had a file operation. So we went over there, and talking, and then he says, let's ___ tell that guy can we get the guy on the same crew? And he says, Okay. He says, Well, fill out the paper, this. Okay. So we get the paper, and after we're done, the next night or what, I ended up in Italy, he ended up in England. You know, it's them Sullivan guys. They didn't want no more five or six getting killed in -- you know, from one family.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. So he went and I -- okay, so I get a letter from my mother that says Nick Tagg was shot down on his 15th mission, they shot him down. The -- had the bombs were still in and everything, destroyed -- it blew him out. The only survivor. It blew him out, he comes to, he's going down. His chute was open and everything. So I don't know where ___.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I met a guy, I think Frank Feriga who knew Nick Tagg.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. He was well-known. And I had a cousin, a Timmy -- Tommy Lanese. He's a Lanese.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What else can you tell me about your training?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Well, we -- we trained in that and this, then I went to -- geez, I went ___ -- we went to Ut -- Texas.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Texas, in what -- I was down there. I don't know. In my papers I got at home, and it says in there you -- I think it said I was -- I had 16 weeks or something.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. So that's -- that's what I knew. Yeah, we go, All right, we're getting assigned, huh?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Given us the assigns to the crew. You'd get the crew and, you know, what the hell we're -- where are we going, he says.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You met your crew in Salt Lake City; is that right?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: That's where they -- that's where we put them together.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: So I got there and we got together. We had to flip a coin. We had two -- three engineers or whatever you want to call them that -- working on the engine.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: So we had too many of them, you know, so we had shorts and -- we had to flip a coin, so who's going to be that or be a -- a radio operator.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. I was a radio -- I said, What the hell, I'm training over here and I'm a radio operator?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you became the radio operator?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, I got -- ___ he was -- he was a character. He was from Texas, and the first time we went out, on our third mission, he -- he was in there when the bombs were going, you know, and they were releasing them, you know, and he went down and then -- and the next -- at night when we'd get in he got a piece of shrapnel in his ass.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: He got hit, because he was looking getting doors open, doors closed, everything. He'd -- and going under. So he says -- first he says -- before that happened, he says, Boy, this is good. I -- he says, I got a good view of the guns and the this and the bombing and the -- okay, he got hit in the ass with that thing, it was a different story, you know. After that, the next day, my -- the door's open, boom. ___+, boom. He slammed that door and went and get the hell out. Because he got down behind the door and he kept it down ___ he ___+.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: That shot that went over that killed his Dutch.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Went over my head. You know, he's taller than me. That damn thing. He was shooting -- we were shooting, I was on that side and shrapnel come in and went over -- went through my window and out the top and -- and it cut the lines, you know, the oxygen. I knew when he came down and hit me, you know.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: So then we -- he -- when I go around there, I rolled him over, I say, Oh, man. Because it went right behind his eye and then knocked his eye out and the eyeball was hanging out, you know. I says, Jesus Christ. So what are you going to do? But, I mean, you know, I say it's destiny or whatever you want to call it, you know? You've got 11 guys over there and you pick out one, that you go -- go ___+ and he's dead. You couldn't pick out one in a million years. That's three -- there was three of them occasions that I seen like that, blown out.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Uh-huh. What kind of planes were you flying?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So when did you go overseas? Was that in --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. It would be on there, that part where the ...

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You were with the 15th Air Corps?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: 99th Bomb Group. Isn't it on there?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I don't see it, but I'm sure it is.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What squadron were you in? Here we go.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: See, I'll recognize the -- I'll hear them and I'll remember them.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Yeah, exactly. I need stronger glasses. So you went over overseas in May. Did you fly overseas?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. And when I was discharged, I come on the ship, you know, because they says -- whenever we're getting discharged, you're getting lined up, got the papers in and everything, and he says, You want to fly or do you want to do it -- this was in November 8th. President Roosevelt then.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: So we -- we got there, he says, Hey, hey, the president got elected, the -- who gives a shit about the president, we need a man ___. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you go straight to Italy then?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I think it was. Yeah, Africa -- what the hell -- ain't that on there? Everything's on there.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Everything's on here, and I need stronger glasses to tell where it is.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Try these. I've got a lot of these glasses. Maybe --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. See, there -- we've got -- everybody here --

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Much better. Arrived Aran (ph), Africa, May 4th,1944; left Aran one week later, May 11th, 1944; arrived in Naples May 15th; went to Magnolia? Is that right?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Maybe that's where we went, yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: -- May 15th; left Magnolia May 18th; arrived Fobia. Is that right, Fobia? Or Fosia?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: No, Fo -- no, that's our main -- it just was --

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Everybody flew out of there, right? Fosia May 19th. That's when you were assigned. Okay. Your first mission of the 27th of May, what do you remember about that first mission?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Well, we -- not much. We enjoyed it, you know. We were all excited about it. You know, it was our first mission, you know, and all that. So ___ the plane, when we got in, it was an iron over there right under me.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You know, over the window, and I put that on there, I says in case something comes up I don't want to crucify me. Yeah, make sure I put that on ___ bullets.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So it looks like that first mission was to France?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. Is that what it says on there?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Do you remember what -- what the target was that day?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Don't it say it on there?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: It doesn't say. It just says May 27th, 1944, France, and I'm not sure what those symbols mean.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Maybe -- do you want me to see?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Yeah, you can go ahead and --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. All right. 8/22, Australia. What are we looking for?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Oh, we -- I was just trying to figure out what the target was in France. What kind of targets were you going after?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Everything. Mostly bombs and big -- bigtime. You know, the oil companies and --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: That's what they tell you is France, Austria -- let's see up here, what have we got? Let's see. Here ___.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Were there any targets you really hated going after?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. Do you see how many of them are in here?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: A lot of them. Yeah, I know they hit that rock, didn't they?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: The bastards. I'll tell you, we -- we done them things and they kept redoing them. We'd go bomb the side, you know, and level the goddamn thing, and then in a month we'd go back, you know, to go look with bombing the other side, you know. They're working on this side, they got the other side fixed. They -- they were doing something ___+. We got through, somebody says we had -- we hit -- they had us set up so we'd hit the one we think we were hitting and we ___. It was like a phony.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And I though holy cri -- we're over there dodging bullets, and, man, them fighters coming in and, whoa. I'll tell you, you know, it's some guy ___, Do you ever feel when you're really ___, you know? I didn't think nothing of it until he mentioned it, you know. Yeah, and I'm thinking I never heard that. I never -- I never really said that. You know, truth be said, I wasn't afraid. Never thought I -- you know, talking and say, Oh, man, you know, we're scared. Geez, oh, man. You know, I was ___, you know that, all excited about it and that, but we made the best of it. What the hell can you do? But it worked out pretty good. I'm glad. Jesus.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So as a waste gunner, did you ever get -- get anything? Did you ever shoot anything?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You don't know if you're the one who got it, right?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Well, yeah. Or ___+. When we get hit with the gang, all them fighter planes out there, he's firing one side, who's the other one, man, you could hear, boom, you look and you see this shrapnel coming through the damn thing, going like hell, and there on the side, we're blasting at them. You know, they say, What did you hit? What the hell, there's 11 guns. Shoot, 11, more than that, who has ___. We're all over that damn sky. And then that color outfit.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. They're ___. I don't care what anybody says, they took care of us. The first mission they did over there, come to take us off, cover for us, they come up, we was talking and he says, Oh, we've got them coming. You know, we go out and look out -- 1 o'clock, here's our cover, you know. Okay. And here they're coming. We're there, he's coming. And he -- our pilot, he -- they're coming right in, the guns towards us. You know, they pointed the guns -- when they come in, they're supposed to come in like this --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: -- you know. Well, they didn't know this, first one. They were coming and kept coming straight, so I ___+. I said, What do you want to do, what do you want to do? He says, Give them a burst, you know. So you're there, he'd face there a little bit, he let it go. Whoa, and they ...

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You know -- well, they didn't -- after that, they were way in the hell out. You could hardly see them. And we were near the end then.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: But they -- they never got us -- you know, had somebody hit us. So there -- you've got to give them credit.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Back to Poleski. Was Poleski -- did they have the -- was that where they had the antiaircraft guns on railroad tracks that they would move them around?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Maybe it wasn't that one. I thought -- I Poleski, they moved them around.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. I was there so many times.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How many do you think, approximately?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Wherever I got them marked in there.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You flew a total of 50 missions?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, 50 -- I don't know what the hell you call it. We did these damn things.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You have to have so many of these when you went through. Let me find it up here. (Pause.)

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I try to remember when the hell these are. Yeah, good luck.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: It's a good thing you have that book, though, then.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So in your 50 missions, all but one of the crew members made it out? You just lost that one crew member?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Were there any other really tough missions that you remember?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, but I don't know where they were, but I know there was another one. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: It doesn't matter where they were. It doesn't matter where, but what do you remember about the mission?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: ___+ got it. We had a -- a gang, you know -- ___ then we had -- we were going to France. ___+ where they had that run into France and hitting France.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: They had the -- you see, some of our ship, it wasn't worth a damn. You know, they turned around for repair.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You seen a couple of them in there.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did that count as a mission?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: No -- well, yeah, you go back.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: If you had to turn around for a mechanical problem?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. If it's something we had to ___. Just didn't take no chances. Them things are in here, I know, but I can't find it.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How many days would you fly before you'd get a break?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: We -- we were -- we flew -- well, whatever it told you here.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You know, every damn day, man.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Well, you must have. You say you started on May 27th.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. I wasn't -- we weren't there that long.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: ___+ You were finished on November 8th, right?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So that was -- that's, what, a little over five months?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you were easily flying at least 10 missions a month.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: We missing our pilot, he -- he broke out with a little rash or something. We were grounded. They didn't know what the hell you get -- didn't go no place. So he was off a couple of days or three days and went back and we went out, but the -- he cut us off with them. And -- what else? Well, I had an episode with Italian, paisan of mine.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: He even had a little dog there. I got some pictures at home. He's got them in the shoe, holding the dog.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Took the dog up when you flew?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: No, he put -- what, put a mask on him?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Uh-huh. I guess that's true. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, he was there. And he started hanging around our tent and he was al -- when we'd come in he was always waiting there. And we -- and then we had this Italian guy that used to come by and buy stuff off of. Buy eggs and bread and wine, you know, ___+ because we'd get -- we'd get a shot after every mission.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: But we wouldn't drink it. You know, we'd save it to get a bottle. What, are we going to have one -- one two shots? This way we had enough to have a party. Yeah. And a guy -- kid from Oklahoma, he'd started shooting -- shooting holes in the tent. Holy criminy, you dumb ass, it's going to rain. He didn't realize it. And they had the ashtrays with the -- that -- the damn -- what hell did we put them in, the candles that lit, and then he went (indicating) and shot that thing out of there. Holy ... So what -- we were all through, this paisan comes. I says, I'm going. Yeah? Yeah. Oh, he looked -- he saw the cigarettes under there, you know, them ones from the World War I, all mildewed, all -- you know, with the -- ___ paisan. Okay, so I got all these supplies free. You know, he took them home. In the morning he comes back, Hey, paisan, look. All ___ went to shit. I said, get -- I had my gun on it. I got -- pull this son of a bitch. We were on a railroad, right behind us was a railroad, and he -- he saw me pulling that and he started running down the railroad, and I fired a couple by their -- on the track, hit the -- hit the reaction. You could hear bing, boom. He ___+ he said 35 cents apiece, that was for -- for breakfast -- eggs.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Eggs. 35 cents apiece I paid for them. That was the end of him.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And one time we had to dig up our floor. We had a wooden floor, we had to dig it up. We had mice under it. So we would hear them running around and running up the -- the ___ the goddamn roof when they were going (indicating).

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: They had to -- we'd go and eat. I'd always get bread or I'd snatch something, take it home for a snack.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And then we had a tank of gas and everything in a dish and we'd have to warm it up for -- at night, have a little snack.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Was your base close to a city or a village?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you go into town on your off days at all?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Got lucky one time. Yeah. Had a wax.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I -- one of the waxers ___ in town, they were on the bus. The bus cut us in. Jesus Christ, pack. You know, they go through the whole area. Jesus. We'd go -- we're loaded in there, man, and go there and we're bouncing and I'm, Oh. There was no place to go. I knew because she'd just got out of the hospital. I saw her the day before, then I caught her ___. We picked her up by her house, I guess, and we stopped, picked my house. So I had her -- so ___ night I was out with her. Pretty good. Pretty good.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you get any shows, any USO shows?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, we got the -- we had all them -- what the hell did you used to call them, the ...

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. Oh, yeah, we had some of that. We had -- what the hell did we have? Somebody else we had.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: We were going down, going to the show, and we were going to the USO or something. What was that ___ that they used to --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. Yeah. So we were going to that. So we were going there. Before we got there, this guy had this girl in there, knocking the shit out of her, slapping her and, you know, they were in the lobby like a --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: This -- the door was set back, you know, it was closed like this.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: So we go by and the guy is slapping her around, you know, and we go over there, you know, grab her -- grab her, grab him, you know, and throw him off. And we get out, the woman, she takes her shoe off, a high heel, she's hitting me over the head. It's her husband. Son of a -- it's her husband. She knocked the shit out of me. ___+ I won't help anybody anymore.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Uh-huh. So there were goofy things happening here. You think you're doing a good thing.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What other missions do you remember? You don't have to tell me where they were.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Just, you know, stories about the missions.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Let me think what ___+ that we had.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. We had a lot of -- you know, we -- like it says in there, the trouble, this or that, or we had -- well, we weren't -- well, we went -- we were -- we were in Italy. We had a bombing in -- ___ it's right at the end of my tongue.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: No, all the way up in the corner, United States. The right end.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Come on, you're around the neighborhood.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Starts with -- starts -- I think it's --

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Well, there is not more Czechoslovakia, so that's --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: ___+. Goddamnit, you know, and you go, Jesus Christ, he ___ there all that time, all them missions and he can't remember? And then all of a sudden I hear it.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: That went from where we ___ station all the way to Czechoslovakia to ___ to a bearing plant, blew that.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And we had to be careful. They topped the gas off before we left, you know, after they cleaned it up and worked it -- warmed it up, ready to go. You save a hundred dollars -- a hundred gallons --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: -- you know, and ____ gas, and you stretch it out. A couple didn't make it. They had to land someplace.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: We had ___ you know, the ___. We made it. Our pilot was -- he was 27 years old, and they thought he was an old man. He was in the infantry, too.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And he got out of there and he wanted to be a pilot and he became a pilot, and a good one. We -- we had a good crew. We'd go -- we went first class in anything. We'd go into town, they'd want to come with us, go to the officers club or ours, we'd take theirs and go, we'd all go. They'd give us one of their shirts, we'd give them one of ours, you know. Sergeant and ___. I was in there, son of a bitch, we were ___ we went in there, here comes a general, stands next to me. I'm there and he -- yes, sir, you know, and I'm standing there and he's taking a leak, you know. I thought, oh, is this guy going to turn around? If he turned around.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. We got away with it.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How many hours was it on that mission to Czechoslovakia?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Oh, it was quite a bit.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Like seven or eight hours or --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: At least. I -- most of the -- all through the day -- usually they're all in the area where it -- you'd come in at 3 o'clock, 3:30, 2 o'clock, 2:30, something like that, 4 o'clock, and then we'd get -- when we'd get there they'd give us a snack, they'd give us Vienna sausage. We'd eat there. Jesus Christ, do they have something else there? You know, and they'd give us that, then we'd go eat when we'd eat, so then it's -- yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Do you have memories of mail call? Did you get much mail from home?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, I got some. Like I say, I got from ____+. He died -- I mean, he -- 15 missions he made. I think that ___ someplace. My mother and my aunts, they'd sent me cookies and all that crap in the boxes.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. I -- like I say, we had one pilot, one assistant, the second chair, and one was from Pennsylvania. The -- he was the engineer -- the -- the ___ gunner we had from New Jersey and one from Oklahoma. He was the one who wanted the ball, ball turret. I says, okay, you can have it.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. He had no trouble getting it, man. That thing is bad news.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You've got to do -- you know, you -- like them guys got blown out or -- they were lucky, but, I mean, you can't fool around with that, because when they say -- they say something ___ gets abandoned the ship over there, you know, of course you've got to get the guns, you've got to turn them, ___ turn, you've got to go up, put your shoes on. By the time you do all that they're hitting the ground.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I mean, that guy done it right. He didn't take no chances. He -- he says they -- they ___ ass ___ bass. Save your bass, I thought he said save your ass.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Then some of them, they're shooting at the pilots, that are dragging the things. They're a mile behind the damn thing, and these guys are -- ___ it and everything. Because -- and they know them -- they'll come and go right through the guy, the pilot. You know, he -- the way they were shooting, I guess, you know, and he'd go right there, raise hell and go -- he got the color, that's how they know.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Your colors. You know, I'm shooting this.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: That's how you keep track of the hits.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And this is what I say. The other way's the same, you know, when you hit somebody. Jesus Christ, they're all shooting at everything. What the hell are you going to do? Yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What do you remember about your last mission?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Oh. Nothing much. I went back on the ship. Well, first we had to wait three -- we waited three or four days it was before we were leaving, you know.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Had -- so that's why I went to Rome. We went up there and them guys says, Hey, you come with us, ___+ Italian and this and that. You know, how -- how he used to do it. I was a brick layer. He used to do it all the time, with all the Italian guys, and I was an apprentice and got them things. And going, You come with us, because he'd be ___. I get up there, their Italian is different than the Italian here. They've got different stages, who's -- where are you from ___, Madrid. ___. So they're getting -- they're getting all of the things in. And we had to ___+. We went in there, man, that place is huge. That's -- the joint, church or whatever you want to call it. This guy was going around, but he says, Take your hat off, put it on that -- it was a -- a bird, a big of some -- a big bird. Bird. And the guy says, You don't realize how big that building is, that church or -- there's a name for it, you'll -- somebody pops it, you'll remember.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Are you talking about the Vatican, you mean?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. And we went, he put that thing on there. It looked -- it looked like it was a big thing, you know. We went in the door, you look at it, it was like this, and go back -- you know, he says, Now, look, what's that thing on? And he says, See that right there? He looks ___ bigger, you know, with that thing in. He says, Jesus, that thing's in there? And it's -- the other one is way bigger. We're like ___ how big that place is. And then up ___+ painted, you know, they painted on their back, years.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah. Yeah. He ___ so then I didn't know what to bring back. We were coming back, so I bought rosaries. I figured, Well, I'll take them, you know, to relatives, aunts and them ___. So I'm trying to count, 15, 20. I think I grabbed 19 or 20 and took them home. I says, I don't want to miss anybody, then I'll never hear the end of it. They'll say, he didn't bring me one, you know?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: So that's -- I marched out with one of them, brought them here. They've still got them hanging around.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So did you get along with the Italian people over there?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: As far as that last mission, it was -- nothing too eventful happened?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: No. We were -- we were glad and everything, you know, but we -- we were all excited. So then they says, You want to -- you want to fly back? No. Hell, no, man. I says, I made it here, now I'm going to get on that plane and crash going home going and go down?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: No, I used up enough coupons. Then I was good on the ship, because I was a sergeant, then, you know, they got bullcrapping with me and we were -- they were bullcrapping and we'd go down there and we'd eat with them. You know, we'd go first class.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: ___ the other ones that were on there. So we ate with them, had -- had anything I wanted, you know. And then we hit a storm. Whoa. That didn't bother me, but, whoa, they got ___ they have a curve around, you know, because with the boat, that stuff is going back and hitting the side, you go in there that side, this side. Whoa. No, thank you. Gee, what else did they do there? Oh, they had a flag on the side, you know ___ and we were in the storm. That thing was day and night. That -- that goddamn ship was bouncing. Huge. I thought holy criminy, what in the hell. Jesus. And when you looked out there, there -- that big thing, it was about this wide from -- just whipped it off, knocked all them things off, off the flag.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you came into the north then?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And I went to New Jersey. And that's where I went, to New Jersey. That's where they released us from, over there. Then I -- ___ after that, when I come back, I knew it was in -- in there for -- in -- in -- I just mentioned the name again. New Jersey.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: New Jersey is where it was on -- in, I should say. Then they sent me to Illinois. They were getting -- you know, at the points, and I was -- I had way enough to get discharged.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And ___ that -- I think I was in Florida and they sent me to Illinois, and then I turned around, I went to -- I -- I tell you, I got a map, a huge map.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And I had -- I got a -- I got up here at -- my daughters, my nephews. You know, they all got these -- who took -- who wanted the medals, who wanted this.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And we had that damn thing, but, Jesus.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So what was your reunion with your family like?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Oh, yeah, they were all glad.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Oh, yeah. We lived it up. And all the boys were home, too, all the -- my gang.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Shoot, we all -- they all wanted to go and -- that whole batch, they -- it was -- I don't know how many of them, they were all -- even up to the end there to now they were all goners, man.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, they all -- two were -- three, he was the one that was a police chief over here, he was a -- he was a ... Ain't this a bitch? All these -- all these months.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, look through there and find -- come up with something.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: A couple days off. Germany, turn back to ___+

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You went to the Isle of -- mission to the Isle of Capris?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: That shows in there. Shows you --

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Rest camp, Isle of Capris. What was that like?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: It looks like you got, what, five or six days there at least.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: You know, then first you had to have 30 -- there were -- you were getting away with 35 --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: -- missions, so then after a while, 35, they figured, Well, things are not so tough anymore, now there ain't that many hits there, you know.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: So we got a lead ship, no ball under it. It was one of the bigshots, they want to see how much damage they -- we got or how much -- how rough it is anymore without the gang and --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: -- all them guys. ___ and so we ___ and -- he was sitting in the radio room. He says, Yeah, he's with a company over here, they want to jack us up to -- higher, just to 50, you know. So, okay, I says, Geez, I hope we wrote a -- we get a good one. You know, wanted to get Vienna or something --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: -- where -- he ___ shit -- shit his pants, man, that -- so we go -- we go over the target, man, we hit it pretty good, too. We were coming through. So on the way back we had room, you know, we were going in there and we were walking around the plane. You know, you could walk, you know. So we'd go around back out there to see what they're doing ___ rear-end and the waste, and we wanted to see how they'd done. There were a few holes in there, in the side, and the radio man says that he -- where he was sitting, there was a -- a hole. It went -- a piece went right through his legs.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: He says -- I says, Oh. He says he turned green. Boy, were we glad. We landed, that guy, he was gone.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: He didn't say nothing good, bad. He -- we never heard no more about it. Probably told them, You want to go sit there, go. So they -- that's how they did, so we went back up.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: What the hell else did we do? Oh, we had a -- we had a lot -- when we would --

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: It says here "easy missions to Italy." The missions to Italy were pretty easy and short?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: They were easy. They weren't damage -- that damage -- they had a few things, but it was no bigtime. But then when I was going to school for all of this, I -- even through on an airplane, like that thing you see out there. I worked -- now, I ___+. I couldn't even find where the hell to turn the key on.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: But what -- I got some of it in and now I forgot everything. Yeah. Them -- we -- our -- it was me and the other two, we were three of us. Our teacher.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: We got her, and she was -- had a lot of fun with us, and we -- she -- some of this, that, wanted us to go get something there. You know, so we got together with her, and her boyfriend used to come up from down in Texas, in -- way down. He was a bigtime -- I don't know if he's still got it going, grand -- plows and all kind of work.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: He's a farmer. He had a farm -- he's a billionaire, he was -- all them things.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And the kid on our crew, his father had a Chevy venture, the war thing in -- in Illinois. He had a big distributor, the -- the company, and when -- after the war, he -- he wanted to come out there -- here and seen us, you know, with the father, he bought some planes off of her --

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: -- you know. So she was there -- her boyfriend would come every Friday, give us his car keys, give us $20 a bill apiece, and we'd go spend the weekend. Every weekend he did. And he was going to take me up -- what the hell did he call them? Mountain oysters or something. Nuts or something. What do you eat, them -- what do you call them things now? The nuts. Yeah. Yeah. But any -- he told us, he says, You never been there? I'm going to take you down there, you know. We went a couple places. Jesus. There's this nice car, Buick. I go myself, a nice -- the two guys with me were -- they were married. Married. He says, Well, we'll hang around tonight, you know. I don't have to hang around, I'm not married. I ___+

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Yeah, yeah, that's right. England. I think they were from England.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I don't know what the hell they done, but they crashed and went down and dragged. Then some of these damn guys had trouble, and they come in and the goddamn things, they had their aerials from their radios with the balls on them outside, they had trouble coming in, and the thing was hanging by them tents.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: And this other one of the damn things, they hit head on. I don't know what the hell happened. Something, they lost control or -- yeah. Jesus.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you were back home when the war ended.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Do you remember any big celebrations on the day the war ended?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: Oh, yeah. We done a lot of things.

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: We would have done them without this -- doing anything. We didn't need anything to have an excuse for something.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So it looks like November 7th, 1944 was your 50th mission.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Do you think that covers it?

sp.speaker: Gaeton Lanese
sp.p: I think. I'll have to start thinking more now, I guess. [End of Interiew]
